cases.name: link
cases.when: href is set -- the item renders an <a href>, which the platform makes a link
cases.reason: There is no link pattern to bind, and that is not an omission: a link's role, its keyboard activation and its focusability all come from the platform the moment the element is an <a href>. Binding `button` here would name a role this element does not have. What the item adds on top of the anchor is `aria-current` for the active destination, which is a clause of the `navigation` pattern SideNav binds, and it is recorded there.

cases.name: button
cases.when: href is absent -- the item renders a <button type="button">, which activates a handler rather than navigating

exceptions.reason: SideNavItem has no disabled concept to reflect: its contract declares `id`, `label`, `icon`, `href` and `activate`, and nothing that would turn a destination off. A navigation item a consumer wants unavailable is one they do not render. This is an absence in the API rather than an unmet requirement in the DOM, and it is declared here so a reader of the binding meets the decision instead of the silence.
